name: CARBON COPIES
clue: Like diamond, this soft gray mineral that fills pencils is an allotrope of pure carbon

name: SHUTTER TO THINK
clue: Her 1936 photograph 'Migrant Mother', shot in a California pea-pickers' camp, became the defining image of the Great Depression.

name: THE $7.2 MILLION QUESTION
clue: Critics branded the 1867 Alaska purchase this Secretary of State's 'folly'; he had survived an assassination attempt the night Lincoln was shot.

name: ISLAND NATIONS
clue: Earth's fourth-largest island is the biggest occupied entirely by a single country that shares its name

name: DATELINE: PACIFIC
clue: In 1995 this island republic bent the International Date Line far eastward so its scattered atolls could all share the same day.

name: CURRENT AFFAIRS
clue: After quizzing his whaling-captain cousin, Benjamin Franklin published one of the first charts of this warm Atlantic current.

name: ANCIENT BATTLES
clue: Octavian's naval victory here in 31 B.C. doomed Antony and Cleopatra and left him master of the Roman world

name: AT THE OPERA
clue: Puccini died before finishing this opera; at its premiere, Toscanini laid down his baton where the composer had stopped

name: LANDLOCKED

name: WORTH ITS WEIGHT
clue: Harvested from crocus stigmas at roughly 150 flowers per gram, this spice has long rivaled gold as the world's costliest.

name: ALOHA MEANS GOODBYE
clue: Deposed in 1893, this last monarch of Hawaii was also a gifted songwriter whose compositions include 'Aloha 'Oe'.

name: UNCONQUERED

name: AGE OF EXPLORATION

name: LINES OF LATITUDE
clue: It's the only country on Earth crossed by both the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn

name: DUTCH MASTERS
clue: Centuries of darkened varnish on his 1642 daytime militia portrait earned it the misleading nickname 'The Night Watch'

name: PROOF POSITIVE
clue: In 1931 this Austrian logician's incompleteness theorems proved that arithmetic contains true statements no formal proof can reach.

name: DRAWING THE LINE
clue: This 1494 treaty drew a meridian through the Atlantic, dividing newly found lands between Spain and Portugal

name: DAYS OF THE WEEK
clue: Thursday belongs to the thunder god Thor; this day of the week honors his one-eyed father

name: AFRICAN COASTLINES
clue: It's the only African nation with shores on both the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean

name: AMERICAN ARCHITECTURE
clue: His only major New York City building, a spiraling Fifth Avenue museum, opened months after his death in 1959

name: DISTANT TOUCHDOWNS
clue: In 2005 the Huygens probe made the most distant landing ever, settling onto this hazy Saturnian moon carved by liquid methane.

name: FINAL EPISODES
clue: Over 100 million Americans watched 'Goodbye, Farewell and Amen,' the 1983 finale of this Korean War sitcom

name: CALENDAR LOGIC
clue: September means 'seventh month' — a name that made sense when the early Roman year began in this month

name: MAJOR TRADITIONS
clue: Unlike golf's other three majors, this tournament returns to the very same course every year

name: DOME IMPROVEMENT

name: TRIPLE CROWN
clue: At a mile and a half, this 'Test of the Champion' is the longest of horse racing's Triple Crown races

name: MEDICAL IMMORTALITY
clue: Cancer cells taken from this Virginia woman without her consent in 1951 became the first immortal human cell line, called HeLa.

name: CAPITAL NAMESAKES
clue: Liberia's capital city honors this U.S. president, whose namesake doctrine warned European powers away from the Americas

name: SEVEN WONDERS
clue: Of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, it's the only one still largely standing today

name: CELL BIOLOGY
clue: These energy-producing organelles carry their own DNA, a genome you inherit only from your mother
